repositories.name: krizaka-build

repositories.name: krizaka-platform-kit
repositories.description: Cross-cutting building blocks for Spring Boot services: stateless JWT security with one baseline, service-to-service tokens, idempotent message consumption and a transactional outbox relay.

repositories.name: krizaka-users
repositories.description: Reusable user management for any application: registration, e-mail verification, login (password + Google/GitHub OAuth), forgot/reset password, profile & preferences, API keys, RBAC and JWT issuance — with its contract (krizaka-users-api) and HTTP client (krizaka-users-client).

repositories.name: krizaka-notifications
repositories.description: Channel-based notification delivery for any application: e-mail (SMTP), SMS (Twilio) and webhooks behind one DeliveryClient port, driven by platform events (user registered, password reset) or explicit notification requests over AMQP.

repositories.name: krizaka-billing
repositories.description: Credits, wallets, plans, subscriptions, a price book and metering (hold → settle → release) as a reusable billing service, with its contract (krizaka-billing-api) and a typed HTTP client (krizaka-billing-client).

repositories.name: orazaka-build

repositories.name: orazaka-contracts

repositories.name: orazaka-studio

repositories.name: orazaka-ai-engine

repositories.name: orazaka-conversation-service

repositories.name: orazaka-job-service

modules.description: The `orazaka` developer CLI: install, start, dev, test, docs and pack tooling for the Orazaka workspace, with an offline SQLite queue.

Next.js (App Router) client of the Orazaka platform with its mandatory BFF.
Automation service — connector execution, CLI-agent dispatch and scheduling (own database)
Orazaka Conversation Service — interactive host (ex-router): HTTP/SSE ingress, job submission and SSE relay
Orazaka Edge Gateway — strangler facade: route table + streaming reverse proxy (transport only, no business logic)
Job Orchestration service — async COMMAND executor (JobListener + strategies) over its own AMQP queues, emitting job lifecycle events
Knowledge service — RAG retrieval + tool source lookup (sync) and async indexing (own database)
Studio service — the marketplace of installable business workflows: catalogue, blueprint versions, installations and run sagas over its own database (ADR-034)
Native (Metal) Python worker for image/video generation and media composition, speaking the Orazaka AMQP worker protocol.
Billing service — credit ledger, hold/settle authorisation, versioned pricebook and entitlements over its own database (ADR-033)
Notification service — renders templates and delivers them through the channel each request names (e-mail, SMS, webhook); stateless, AMQP-driven
Identity service — the trust root: authN, RBAC, profile, credentials, API keys (hosts the krizaka-users-core + persistence-identity libraries)

Tier-2 SDK — envelope encryption for the asset store: a per-file data key wrapped by a master key nobody but a key provider ever sees, block-addressable so a Range request decrypts one block instead of a file
Orazaka Decoupled Application Persistence & Infrastructure State Management

Platform bridge library: package-private @Service adapters that implement the core's DB-backed outbound ports (CapabilityProvider, PipelineConfigProvider, PlatformToolConfigProvider, PlatformMcpServerProvider, UserMcpServerProvider, ValidationPipelineRepository) by delegating to the orazaka-persistence-app-api inbound ports. Bundled by every service that runs the cognitive pipeline in-process (conversation-service, job-service, …) so the shared core beans wire without each service re-implementing the same DB adapters. Discovered via the hosts' com.krizaka.orazaka component scan — no HTTP surface, no entrypoint.

Tier-2 SDK — the consumer side of the Studio contract: a NoOp and an HTTP adapter for StudioRunClient and StudioCatalogClient, selected at bootstrap so no call site branches on whether the marketplace is deployed
Tier-2 SDK — the producer side of the billing contract: a NoOp and an HTTP adapter for CreditAuthorizationClient, selected at bootstrap so no call site ever branches on whether billing exists

Typed HTTP client of the users service's internal API (UserDirectoryClient): user, profile, provider keys and rate-limit tiers, authenticated with a SERVICE token and cached per entry. A Spring Boot auto-configuration.
Orazaka User and Identity Persistence Block
Business persona prompts and PromptOps content resolver — pure library module

Single interceptor pipeline module — packages by concern: security, token, context, translation, enrichment, reformulation, tooling, validation, governance (AGENTS.md §7, VISION_ARCHITECTURE §6). Registered via @AutoConfiguration SPI.
Orazaka Tools and MCP Implementations
Orazaka AI Orchestration Engine
Orazaka Identity and Access Management Domain

Job-plane contract (ADR-037) — the JobCommand wire record every producer and executor shares, and the capability routing port that turns "where does this capability run" into a row; pure JDK, no dependencies

Tier-1 contract of the persistence-app context: the inbound port interfaces + DTOs the cognitive core and hosts depend on. Pure — no JPA, no entities, no DB driver; the only outside type is Spring Data's Page/Pageable pagination abstraction.
Studio marketplace contract (ADR-034) — the catalogue, blueprint DAG, installation and run types every context composes against; pure JDK, no dependencies
Billing and entitlements contract (ADR-033) — the credit hold/settle ports and DTOs every producer on the hot path depends on; pure JDK, no dependencies
Notification contract — the request a producer publishes, the delivery channels and the AMQP routing it travels on; pure JDK, no dependencies
Identity principal contract (the User record) — the only identity type downstream services keep after the Phase 2 extraction; pure JDK, no dependencies

At-least-once messaging done right for Spring Boot and RabbitMQ: events published through a transactional outbox with their envelope in AMQP headers, a relay that claims what it publishes, consumer queues with retry and a dead-letter queue by convention, and idempotent consumption (an atomic claim, released when the handler fails).

One observability standard for Spring Boot services: every service names itself (product, service, version) or does not start, its metrics carry those names as common tags, and the defaults every service repeats — ECS JSON console logs, health/info/prometheus exposed, 10% trace sampling — are set once, at the lowest priority.

Stateless JWT security for Spring Boot services: the shared HS256 session-token decoder, the roles-claim authority mapping, one security baseline (CORS preflight, health, error page, SERVICE-only internal surface) and the service-to-service token.

The Krizaka observability standard in one dependency: krizaka-observability (required service names, common metric tags, ECS logs, exposure and sampling defaults) with Actuator, OpenTelemetry tracing over OTLP and a Prometheus registry.

Events and consumers over RabbitMQ in one dependency: krizaka-messaging (outbox publishing, consumer queues with retry then DLQ, idempotent consumption) with Spring AMQP, JDBC and Jackson. Add your JDBC driver.
Stateless JWT security in one dependency: krizaka-security (HS256 session tokens, roles authorities, the security baseline, service tokens) with Spring Security and its OAuth2 resource server.
HTTP service baseline in one dependency: krizaka-web (Problem Details, request correlation, Jackson defaults, cursor pagination, declared CORS) with Spring MVC, bean validation and Actuator.

The HTTP baseline of a Spring Boot service, written once: RFC 9457 Problem Details with stable error codes, X-Request-Id correlation into the MDC, Jackson 3 defaults, opaque cursor pagination and declared CORS origins.
